title: The indigo weighs less
body: Rahel offers you a sack of indigo, a blue dye, and says how much it weighs. Your clerk weighed a sample, and it comes out lighter. She says your scales are wrong. Your clerk says hers are.

choices.label: Weigh it again at the market
choices.hint: A weigher takes a small fee.

choices.label: Split the difference with her
choices.hint: Rahel will remember a fair offer.

choices.label: Say no and buy elsewhere
choices.hint: You buy elsewhere and gain 4 in two seasons, and other sellers hear of it.

note: In one of Cairo's markets a weigher, called a qabbani, weighed coins and goods for a fee.

sources.at: n. 80; the qabbani at the market of Harat al-Barjawan, undated

title: Two partners, one share
body: Idris and Binyamin put money into a venture together. Each says he put in more. Their own ledger says they paid the same. They ask your house, which keeps honest books, to settle it.

choices.label: Split it evenly, as the ledger says
choices.hint: Both are a little unhappy now. A fair count earns respect later.

choices.label: Pay each what he claims
choices.hint: It costs you. Generous houses are remembered.

choices.label: Take it to a judge
choices.hint: The judge takes a fee, and his word is final.

note: Merchants had long done much of their overseas trade through partnerships. Partnerships between Jews and Muslims were nothing unusual.

sources.at: pp. 11 to 12, as quoted by Edwards and Ogilvie (2008), p. 11
pp. 72 and 172 to 173, as quoted by Edwards and Ogilvie (2008), p. 17

title: Samir counts his share again
body: Samir is home from {to}. He says your clerk counted what he is owed 5 dinars too low. Your clerk says the cost of the trip comes off first. Samir kept no book, but he remembers every sale.

choices.label: Pay the 5 dinars he asks for
choices.hint: It costs a little. Samir will go again gladly.

choices.label: Keep your clerk's count and take back 4 for the trip's costs
choices.hint: You gain 4 dinars. Samir will not forget it.

note: In the Geniza contracts the traveller's share was normally one third. Partners made up their accounts every year, and a quarrel over the sums could end in a judge's court.

sources.at: p. 317; the worker's share, normally one third
pp. 326 to 327; court records of a quarrel over sums, and the yearly accounts

title: Ali and the price
body: Ali is home from {to}. Your clerk thinks Ali sold too cheaply. The house made less than the sheet hoped. Ali says the prices were fair and that he did it for the house.

choices.label: Make Ali pay what he can
choices.hint: You win back 7 dinars. Ali is bitter.

choices.label: Share the loss with him
choices.hint: You win back 4 dinars. He promises to keep to his orders.

choices.label: Forgive him and write stricter orders
choices.hint: You win nothing back now, and it costs 2 dinars in two seasons. Ali is grateful.

note: In the Geniza papers contracts said where an agent could trade. An agent who went beyond them and lost money paid the whole loss himself.

sources.at: p. 327; a manager who broke the conditions of the contract

title: Two judges for one quarrel
body: Jabir is Muslim and Ezra is Jewish. Each put money into the same venture, and now they quarrel over 20 dinars. Each wants his own judge. Your house is asked to say where they go.

choices.label: Ask the Muslim judge to call in a Jewish judge
choices.hint: It costs two fees. Both men will trust the answer.

choices.label: Send them to one judge only
choices.hint: It costs one fee. One of them will feel slighted.

choices.label: Settle it yourselves over a meal
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars, and the street likes a quarrel ended. It may come back.

note: In one case from the Geniza papers a Muslim judge asked a Jewish judge to help. The quarrel was between a Muslim and a Jew. The case is not dated. Edwards and Ogilvie report it from the historian Moshe Gil.

sources.at: p. 18, citing Gil 2003, pp. 281 to 282 (not read); the Muslim judge who asked for the Jewish judge
